variants.mechanism: The two actual source stars in the same column but separated by an intervening club cell are paired by red and blue outlines with the two adjacent stars in option C. This targets treating selected parts as an adjacent domino while overlooking their true one-cell separation and unequal star orientations. It binds input symbols to candidate symbols rather than highlighting an option in isolation.

variants.primary_unique_math: A legal piece is one pair of orthogonally adjacent unit cells, transformed rigidly. B is exactly the top-row upright star and upright club immediately to its right (column2 to3). A requires an upright star with an upright spade immediately to its right, absent in the grid; the lower star is itself rotated20 degrees and cannot become an upright star under the quarter-turns allowed by cell adjacency. C requires adjacent stars, but the only two stars are separated by one club cell. D requires the shown downward heart followed by a vertical diamond; the neighboring heart/diamond at the bottom left does not have the required orientation relative to its connecting line. E has two horizontally adjacent downward hearts; the two identical downward source hearts are vertically adjacent, so a quarter-turn makes both point sideways. Enumerating all24 undirected board-adjacencies in both orders and the four grid-preserving rotations, with the visible symbol orientations, matches only B. Source cells, all symbol contours, rotations, and fills are unchanged.
variants.approval_status: No Pass/Collect; not delivered; no independent review performed by author.
limitations: No original control was run; two calls alone do not prove the marks caused either error.
No human performance measurement or per-marker ablation; neither is an added hard gate.
Run1 explicitly rejects colored C adjacency and finally selects E. Run2 selects C after treating colors as symbol identity and hallucinating adjacent stars. One C hit does not count as two.

This targets accepting a nearly matching ordered part by binding its mismatched third ray to the wrong white partner. All semantic shades and lengths remain explicit.
